%: The top of the winding stair. Down to the hall.
2: A door painted the same grey as the wall. Not hidden, exactly. Just hoping you won't notice it.
3: Double doors, black and gold, with his face carved on both. On the left door he's smiling. On the right he's smiling more.
=: A long runner, threadbare in a line down the middle. Someone paces here. A lot.
W: Black stone. Somebody has hung a little embroidered sampler on it: HOME SWEET HOME. It is not convincing.
B: The fist crushing a crown, again. He really likes that one.
c: A torch, and beside it, a bucket of sand. Someone in this house worries about fires.
F: A hearth, burning low. Five chairs drawn up to it, and a footstool nobody admits is theirs.
w: A wardrobe, carved with fists and crowns. Inside: fur, more fur, and a crown that's slightly too small.
y: A vanity, with five sets of combs. They are labelled.
n: Tea for five. Everyone's cup is half full. Nobody has touched the biscuits. Nobody wants to look like they want the biscuits.
f: A portrait of Kaldor, with a different queen in each corner. Somebody has drawn a little crown over one of them in ink.
Q: A great bed with red curtains. It's been made so tightly a coin would bounce off it.
D: His journal, open. The last pages, in a big square hand:
'No word from my master. A hundred years now. I take it as trust.'
'The French one says the wizards are weak. The French one says many things.'
'Asked the chandelier about the war. It agrees with me.'
6: A note on the desk in looping handwriting: 'Room 3. The bed is too soft, the view too grey, the king too loud. Five stars. — F'
z: A chessboard, mid-game. The white king is surrounded. One black piece is missing.
K: A child's cot, under a dust sheet. A wooden sword lies in it, carved with one letter: B.
Nobody has slept here in five hundred years. Nobody has cleared it out, either.
7: A tiny suit of armour on a stand. A prince's. It has been polished recently, and not by a servant.
9: A little writing desk, child-height. In the drawer, under a tin soldier: a journal, in a boy's careful hand.
'I never wanted to be king. I never wanted power. But it appears Mother and Father want me to go to war. They say it is for the good of the kingdom. My art teacher disagrees.'
'Everyone does what they think is best for them. People get wants and needs confused.'
'They're my parents, and I know I must honour their wishes. But at the cost of how many lives? I've never taken a life before.'
8: A small carved horse on rockers, the paint long gone. Its name is burned into the saddle: SIR GALLOP.
U: The winding stair, turning down into the hall.
h: A thick rug from somewhere far away. Kaldor's army brought back a great many rugs.

objects.name: Queen Brunhilt
lines: Oh! A visitor. Sit, sit. You've come about him, haven't you. Everyone comes about him.

answer: QUEEN BRUNHILT: Oh, where to start.

QUEEN HELKA: Five hundred years of 'tomorrow we march'. I have heard 'tomorrow' more than I have heard my own name.
QUEEN MAREN: That is my loving husband you are talking about.
QUEEN HELKA: She only says that because she's the favourite.
QUEEN MAREN: I am not the favourite.
QUEEN BRUNHILT: You have the good room.
QUEEN MAREN: ...I have the good room.

QUEEN ASTRA: Between us? If somebody were to knock him down a peg, we would not be heartbroken.
QUEEN MAREN: I would be a little heartbroken.
QUEEN HELKA: The favourite.

questions.ask: First queen, and you got the worst room?
